svg.title: WHAT A HUB SOLVES
svg.desc: Comparison of three district depots without a hub and one charging hub serving the same districts. One: three separate grid upgrades versus one shared upgrade. Two: districts pay the utility side upfront and wait for refunds, while at hub scale utilities often pay, 9 million dollars in Brooklyn and 2.7 MW in Oakland. Three: peak draw of about 10 kW per bus versus about 2 kW with managed charging, from New York City’s modelling. Four: chargers installed site by site versus in about four weeks above ground in Brooklyn. Five: districts buy their chargers versus a monthly fee to the operator, which owns the chargers (company-stated). The size of the saving is not published.
svg.text: The same three districts, without a hub and with one. Five things the hub changes.
Each district electrifies its own depot
One bus company’s yard serves all three
Charging hub · Districts A, B and C

First, one grid upgrade instead of many. Without a hub, every depot needs its own. A hub needs one, shared by many
